document_metadata.title: Gold Data for training of Sanskrit Corpus
document_metadata.subject_english: Nature of Root and Affix (Prakrti and Pratyaya)
document_metadata.purpose: Gold data for training Sanskrit corpus and NLP models

introduction.core_concept: The continuous flow of vowels and consonants constitutes language or speech or literature
introduction.original_sutra: स्वरव्यञ्जनयोः समीच्चोरणमेव भाषणम् अथवा भाषा अथवा वाङ्मयम् भवति

svara.definition: Any of the vowel sounds in Sanskrit

vyanjana.definition: Any of the consonant sounds in Sanskrit

sequence_patterns: sv_sv_vy (स्व स्व व्य - vowel vowel consonant)
vy_sv_vy (व्य स्व व्य - consonant vowel consonant)
sv_vy_sv_vy (स्व व्य स्व व्य - alternating pattern)
sv_vy_vy_sv_vy_sv_vy (स्व व्य व्य स्व व्यस्व व्य)
sv_sv_sv_vy_sv_vy_vy_vy (स्व स्व स्व व्य स्व व्य व्य व्य - et cetera)

need_for_grammar.problem: The sequence of vowels and consonants has no fixed rules in natural speech; only native speaker competence provides intuition
challenges: Natural speech changes over time and place
Without grammar, ancient literature becomes incomprehensible
grammar_function: Enables extraction of full intention of the speaker
Helps listeners decode meaning correctly and meaningfully
Preserves language form and prevents arbitrary changes due to time and place

vyakarana_subject_matter.definition: Sacred scholarly meanings and words formulated by grammar experts for conducting grammatical operations and comprehensive understanding of language
vyakarana_subject_matter.original_sutra: अत्र शास्त्रज्ञैः शास्त्रप्रक्रियानिर्वाहाय, भाषायाः समग्रपरिशीलनाय च केचन अलौकिकाः (शास्त्रीयाः) अर्थाः, शब्दाश्च परिकल्पिताः

primary.name: धातुः
primary.description: The fundamental semantic unit from which verbal forms are derived

primary.name: प्रातिपदिकम्
primary.description: The fundamental unit for nominal words

primary.name: प्रत्ययः
primary.description: Brings specific meaning to the root or stem

three_primary_components.note: The first two are collectively called 'Prakrti' (Root/Stem) - the base from which the modified form arises through affixation

dhatu_roots.definition: A combination of vowels and consonants by which a particular action is understood
dhatu_roots.devanagari_definition: धातुः नाम तादृशः स्वरव्यञ्जनयोः राशिः येन क्रिया काचित् बोध्यते

varieties.english: Roots listed in Dhatupath (dictionary of roots)
varieties.example: Primary roots as per traditional lists
कृ (to do) → कारि (to cause to do)

pratipadika_nominal_stems.definition: A meaningful combination of vowels and consonants that is distinct from roots, distinct from affixes, distinct from affix-endings
pratipadika_nominal_stems.complete_definition: Each word, each occurrence, each state (bhava) constitutes a pratipadika (nominal stem)
characteristics: Word form (shabda-svarupa) - combination of vowels and consonants
Distinct from roots, affixes, and affix-endings

types.name: सञ्ज्ञारूपं प्रातिपदिकम्
types.description: Pratipadika in the form of proper nouns or substantives
types.characteristic: These are nominal forms designated as pratipadika

types.name: कृदन्तप्रातिपदिकम्
types.description: Stem ending in a krt (derivational) affix
types.detailed_definition: After a root, a krt-affix is provided for agent, object, etc. purposes. The word-form ending in this suffix becomes a pratipadika

example.note: This uninhibited utterance of root + affix is called 'krd-vrtti' (krt-function)

types.name: तद्धितान्तप्रातिपदिकम्
types.description: Stem ending in a taddhita (secondary derivational) affix
types.detailed_definition: A taddhita-affix is provided after a nominal (subanta) for offspring, relationship etc. purposes. The word-form ending in this affix becomes a pratipadika

example.note: This uninhibited utterance of nominal + taddhita-affix is called 'taddhita-vrtti' (taddhita-function)

types.name: समाससञ्ज्ञकं प्रातिपदिकम्
types.description: A word designated as a compound

example.common_meaning: The husband of Sita as seen in the world
example.note: The combination of two nominal words with non-interrupting utterance

types.name: अव्ययसञ्ज्ञकं प्रातिपदिकम्
types.characteristic: These forms are designated as indeclinable (avyaya) in grammar and still function as pratipadika

pratyaya_affixes.definition_in_other_texts: In other sciences, pratyaya means knowledge
pratyaya_affixes.grammar_definition: In grammar, pratyaya is a meaningful Vowel or combination of vowels and consonants

nature_of_meaning.what_kind: A specific meaning (not seen separately in the world)
characteristics: Universally appears in words of the same category (sva-jatiya)
Both non-universal (unique to world) and universal (across all similar words)
Often accompanied by any other letter for grammatical process

pratyaya_affixes.function: Each affix typically has marks and signals indicating other grammatical tasks

example.semantic_function: The trich affix is devised to express the agent meaning across all these forms

pratyaya_classification.introduction: Affixes are classified into eleven types based on semantic functions

eleven_types.english: Affixes causing transformation of one verbal root to another verbal root (Sanadi affixes like nic, san, yan)
eleven_types.description: Change one action (verbal root) to another action

subnote.context: Sometimes affixes occur after finite verb forms (तिङन्तs)

eleven_types.english: Affixes causing transformation of verbal root to nominal form (Krt affixes)
eleven_types.description: Change a verbal root to a noun/name

eleven_types.english: Affixes causing transformation of verbal root to indeclinable/adverbial form
eleven_types.description: Change a verbal root to an indeclinable (adverbial modifier)

eleven_types.english: Affixes causing transformation of nominal to verbal root
eleven_types.description: Change a nominal/noun to a verbal root

example.english_result: putríya (to act as a son - a verbal root)

eleven_types.english: Affixes causing transformation of one nominal to another nominal form (Taddhita affixes)
eleven_types.description: Change one noun to another noun (secondary derivation)

example.english_result: dasharathi (descendant of Dasharatha - another noun form)

eleven_types.english: Affixes causing transformation of nominal to indeclinable form
eleven_types.description: Change a nominal to an indeclinable

eleven_types.english: तिङ् affixes - causing transformation of any verbal root to finite verb form
eleven_types.description: Finite verb conjugation affixes that express person, number, tense

example.note: All verbal roots take तिङ् affixes in various forms

eleven_types.english: Sup affixes - causing transformation of any pratipadika to nominal form (case declension)
eleven_types.description: Nominal case declension affixes expressing number, case, gender
Affixes related to compound word formation
Affixes that serve special semantic purposes (some are categorized within other divisions); found throughout various classifications

ashtadhyayi_classification.introduction: These eleven types of affixes are distributed in the Ashtadhyayi (Panini's grammar)

distribution.name: सनादिप्रत्ययाः
distribution.description: Affixes like nic, san, yan etc. that modify verbal roots

distribution.name: कृत्प्रत्ययाः
distribution.description: Affixes derived from verbal roots; includes lad, तिङ् conjugations

ashtadhyayi_classification.note: तिङ्-प्रत्ययेs come under कृत्-प्रत्ययs and reflexive affixes (svarthika-pratyaya) are distributed throughout all these categories

prakrti_root_stem.definition: The prakrti (root/stem) is the limit/boundary for every affix
prakrti_root_stem.explanation: The prakrti is that word-combination from which the affix is formed; it is also called 'anga' (limb/part)
prakrti_root_stem.manifestation: As affixes manifest in eleven ways, prakrti also manifests in eleven corresponding ways
prakrti_root_stem.classification: Prakrti can be classified into the same eleven categories as affixes based on their function

pratyaya_mala_chain.key_point: Some affixes arise from roots without any affixes; some arise from roots with one affix; some arise with multiple affixes

step_1.english: bhav (causative root - to cause to be)

step_2a.english: bhavayati (causes to be - 3rd person singular present)

step_2.meaning: The state of causing to be
step_2.note: Further derivation from this nominal form

pratyaya_chains_comprehensive.introduction: Various combinations of roots, affixes and their chains in world and Vedic usage

possible_chains.description: Root becomes nominal, then secondary derivation, then declension
Root modified for causative, then desiderative, then nominalized

possible_chains.chain: धातुः + सन् + णिच्/यङ्/क्यच्/क्यङ्/यक् + कृत् + स्त्री + सुप्
possible_chains.english: Root + San + Various affixes + Krt + Feminine + Sup

possible_chains.description: Nominal form, case marking, secondary derivation, case marking

possible_chains.chain: प्रातिपदिकम् + स्त्री + सुप् + तद्धित + स्त्री + सुप्
possible_chains.english: Pratipadika + Feminine + Sup + Taddhita + Feminine + Sup

pratyaya_chains_comprehensive.conclusion: In these manifold ways, affixes appear in the world and in the Vedas based on usage; one must understand this

affix_usage_constraints.key_principle: Not all possible affix combinations are used in practice
affix_usage_constraints.constraint_1: Apada na prayunjita (One should not use 'apada' - non-word forms)
application: One should not use only a root (prakrti) alone
One should not use only an affix (pratyaya) alone
Every utterance must be a complete word (pada)
affix_usage_constraints.pada_definition: A pada is a word form that is either:
affix_usage_constraints.determination_requirement: One must know: What word is produced? What portion/part constitutes the word? Only then can segmentation be done correctly anywhere in literature
affix_usage_constraints.principle: Only complete words are used in speech; never incomplete formations

sup_affixes_nominal_declension.description: Sup is a special designation by which the following affixes are indicated
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.english_enumeration: su, au, jas, am, aUT, shas, TA, bhyAm, bhis, Nge, bhyAm, bhyas, Ngsi, bhyAm, bhyas, Ngas, os, Am, Ngi, os, sup
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.total_count: Twenty-one affixes included in the term 'sup'
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.function: These affixes are applied to pratipadika to express agent and other meanings
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.system: The abbreviation 'sup' is a pratiharya (substitute term) in which twenty-one affixes are embedded
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.organization: The distribution is based on three affixes (triplet system) for different numbers and cases
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.triplets: Seven triplets, each triplet showing singular, dual, plural forms
sup_affixes_nominal_declension.case_marking: Each triplet represents different cases marked with different number-based endings

case_system_detailed.introduction: The seven-case system with three numbers
case_system_detailed.system_description: Three markers for singular, dual, plural within each of seven cases
case_system_detailed.organizational_principle: The seven cases are distinguished by specific affixes and marks
case_system_detailed.naming_scheme: First case of a triplet gets duplication; after duplication, the second triplet gets the name 'sambodhan-prathama' (vocative-nominative)
case_system_detailed.number_system: Within each triplet, there are three divisions:
case_system_detailed.principle: The appropriate affix must be chosen based on the pratipadika and the number concept involved
case_system_detailed.result: All words form correctly from their respective pratipadika through this system

components.english: Participial combination of vowels-consonants designated as pratipadika
combination of sounds designated as affix
Sound-combination that is a substitute for the affix
Vowel that is a substitute for pratipadika and affix
Sound that is a substitute for the substitute

worked_example_ramen.result: रामेण इति सूबन्तं पदम् (ramena is a declined nominal word)

तिङन्त_finite_verbs.description: तिङ् is a special designation indicating verbal affixes
तिङन्त_finite_verbs.english_enumeration: tip, tas, jhi, sip, thas, tha, mip, vas, mas, ta, AtAm, jha, thAs, AthAm, dhvam, iD, vahi, mahin
तिङन्त_finite_verbs.meaning: The combination of vowels and consonants derived from root + तिङ्-affix with substitutions and modifications
derivation_sequence: भू + अ + ति (substitution of shap with 'a')
तिङन्त_finite_verbs.result: भवति इति तिङन्तपदम् (bhavati is a finite verb word)

word_formation_principle.core_principle: A meaningful combination of vowels and consonants that is produced through combination of pratipadika/dhatu with sup/तिङ्-affix including substitutions and augments
word_formation_principle.hidden_elements: In worldly language, substitutions and augments are typically invisible/not directly observable; they operate according to established rules on dhatu/pratipadika
word_formation_principle.principle: This system represents the extraordinary genius of Paninian grammar, allowing comprehensive understanding of Sanskrit morphology

grammatical_constraints.english: One should not use non-word forms (apada)
application: Neither only prakrti (root/stem) alone should be used
Nor only pratyaya (affix) alone should be used
Only forms that are either subanta or तिङन्त should be used
These represent complete, meaningful words in usage
grammatical_constraints.methodology: Therefore, words themselves are what we use in speech
grammatical_constraints.usage_rule: Words are what should be used in speech

research_methodology.observation: Through examination of all sound variations heard in worldly usage
research_methodology.procedure: Scholars carefully analyzed these sound variations to formulate the concepts of dhatu, pratipadika, etc.
research_methodology.purpose: To understand the underlying structure that produces observable linguistic phenomena
research_methodology.application: The grammatical framework enables extraction of complete meaning and prevents arbitrary language change over time
